Energy reduction and novelty remain unproven. No board has been programmed or electrically measured.
2.8: head candidate 4,160/5,280 cells; 19.3858566 MHz routed estimate. Full pipeline 6,575/5,280, rejected.
8×8 handwritten digits; each pixel encoded using three thresholds, giving 192 input bits per image.
Truth tables, differentiable formulas, and Verilog expressions implemented. Gate tests pass.
Soft gate selection, fixed connections, and class-score calculation implemented.
4 layers × 1,000 gates, 60 epochs, seed 0, switching penalty disabled.
1.5 Lock each gate to one rule
Soft: 93.78%; hard: 93.56%; loss from discretization: 0.22 percentage points.
NumPy implementation computes gate outputs, integer class scores, and predictions. Hard PyTorch scores match it.
Input/output registers, logic layers, score calculation, predicted class, and valid signals generated.
1.9 Generate reference vectors and a self-checking testbench
Testbench compares every class score and the predicted class against Python.
1.10 Verify the trained model in simulation
450/450 images match exactly. This covers those inputs; it is not formal verification over every possible input.
45 tests pass: 14 earlier cases, 16 independently written exhaustive head-pipeline cases, 11 artifact and 4 data-partition cases. See independent review for scope.
2.1 Synthesize the original design for iCE40
2,929 LUT4s, 268 flip-flops, 123 carry cells. Latency: 2 cycles.
Added registers after each of the four logic layers. Latency: 6 cycles.
450/450 images match exactly, including scores and predictions.

Selected iCE40UP5K/SG48 and Yosys → nextpnr-ice40 → IceStorm. Installed nextpnr/IceStorm; counter check passed synthesis, placement/routing, 12 MHz timing, and bitstream generation. Run bash synth/check_ice40_flow.sh. This does not establish DLGN timing or board operation.
Historical UART interfaces verified. Current corrected head candidate fits and meets 12 MHz; full-layer candidate remains oversized. See 2.8.

Explicit 12 MHz SDC clock plus all four PCF pins accepted by nextpnr. Mapped RX/reset synchronizer connections checked; no timing exceptions. Packing checked for both versions. See step 2.7 learning note for scope and capacity result.

Original routed but failed 12 MHz (7.26 MHz estimate). Corrected head-only pipeline/atomic-input candidate routes at 12 MHz using 4,160/5,280 cells; independently reproduced. Current full-layer+head candidate needs 6,575 cells and cannot fit.

Corrected candidate has a 19.3858566 MHz routed estimate at the fixed 12 MHz target. Other full-layer candidate is oversized. Consolidated scope/performance reporting and physical validation remain distinct.
Report clock frequency, latency in cycles and time, and predictions per second for both architectures.
3.1 Count logical gate changes in Python
Baseline average: 0.34976 changes per gate per image transition, using the saved test order.
DUMP=1 support exists in the simulator script and testbench. No saved VCD waveform was found.
Run the original design with waveform recording enabled and preserve the input sequence.
Count signal transitions, avoid counting aliases twice, and handle unknown values explicitly.
Exclude reset and startup; account for pipeline fill and drain so comparisons cover equivalent useful work.
Report logical-layer activity separately from registers, clock, control, and output logic where observable.
Compare corresponding settled logical outputs under the same image order. Explain discrepancies.
Extend beyond logical gates to signals in the synthesized or implemented design.
Use an appropriate timing-aware simulation flow if supported. Ordinary RTL traces cannot establish physical glitch activity.

Code supports λ × mean[2p(1−p)], an IID zero-delay surrogate. One-epoch smoke validates execution only; effectiveness and energy correlation remain untested. Future runs use validation monitoring and saved partitions/checkpoints.
Existing run uses λ = 0 and has saved accuracy, model, and logical switching results.

Retrain both lambda=0 and lambda>0 with the same 1,077 train / 270 validation / 450 test split, architecture and settings. Select using validation. Historical 93.56% baseline is exploratory and used a different protocol.
Compare several λ values using validation data for selection; reserve test results for final evaluation.
Check that improvements are reproducible rather than dependent on one initialization.
Export each model and repeat score-and-class comparisons against its own Python reference.
4.7 Measure each model’s hardware cost and activity
Compare accuracy, switching, LUTs, registers, and timing using a consistent procedure.
Accuracy versus switching first; accuracy versus estimated or measured energy once available.
Per-sample penalty mode exists, but no experiment has compared it with the batch-mean switching penalty.
Confirm the FPGA target, software, and activity-file format. The notes propose Vivado for detailed power analysis, but this is not configured.
Import simulation activity and check which implemented signals receive it and which use tool defaults.
Record operating conditions and report static and dynamic power separately, including the tool’s component breakdown.
Use the same target, clock, workload, and analysis settings as the baseline.
Divide the stated power quantity by sustained predictions per second; distinguish total energy from dynamic-only energy.
Quantify energy reduction alongside accuracy, area, and performance changes. No energy reduction has been demonstrated yet.
Notes list an iCEBreaker/iCE40 UP5K; physical availability and connection have not been checked in this session.
FPGA UART adapter and packet format implemented; a serial host client and live connection remain pending.
UART pins, board reset, image assembly, core inference, and serial results pass end-to-end simulation. Host integration and physical-board checks remain pending.
Complete board-specific constraints, placement/routing, timing checks, and programming.
Send known test images and record exact prediction agreement.
Identify measurement equipment and whether we can measure an FPGA supply rail or only whole-board power.
Run identical workloads and record power, runtime, and predictions for baseline and optimized designs.
Project context (docs/PROJECT_CONTEXT.md) contains the verified baseline and architecture comparison.
Collect configuration, seed, accuracy, switching, resources, timing, and power into a consistent results table.
Local models and logs exist, but runs/ is gitignored. Decide how final artifacts will be archived.
MNIST loading and training support exist; no saved MNIST experiment was found. Larger experiments follow the working baseline.
7.5 Prepare the final report, plots, slides, and demo
Recorded final submission/presentation date: December 4, 2026. Existing proposal materials were not found in this repository.
